about: The campaign's opening titles (design/opening-titles.md). Built one step at a time from the start of the video; shots not yet in `built` show the source in drafts.

preroll.note: Before frame 0: the set flicks through two empty channels (static), lands on the VCR's blue screen, PLAY is pressed and the tape plays with its tracking off, the TRACKING meter hunts, and it locks to black. Ingram: "start with a 'tracking issue' and add some blank space, just a few seconds", and "do the VHS text on the screen too... as if it were changing channel". Its frames are numbered -72 to -1; sound times are seconds from its first frame.

clips.note: Two empty channels of static, with a frame of black as the set changes between them.
The VCR's own blue screen: the set is on the tape's channel and nothing is playing yet.
The tape playing, its tracking off: static bands roll up the black until the meter settles and it locks, then a little over half a second of clean black before the programme.
The set's channel number, flicking up to the tape's channel.
PLAY, pressed two frames before the tape's picture arrives; it clears half a second before the programme, leaving clean black.
The tracking meter hunting down, overshooting, and settling back on the middle as the picture locks.
The tiny blue point at dead centre through the black leader; it dims after the flare.
One frame: the raindrop's fat flat ring (measured: fill 43,155,252; radius 139 to 234; edge wobble).
The splash crown: 58 droplets just inside the donut's inner edge (measured count).
The four-point sparkle at the donut's centre (measured peak 163,242,255).
The ring spreading and slowing, re-timed to the source's holds; it stays near-continuous and gets thinner, dimmer and finely speckled (a fine dash mask, not big arcs).
The thin dashed line just inside the ring on its first two drawings.
The soft halo the source's painted rings carry.
The raindrop lands: a white dot (measured centre 703,551).
The main ring (measured radii 107, 228, 484), then out past the frame.
The second ring, drifting down and right as it grows (measured 717,615 r49 -> 760,663 r129 -> 923,931 r319).
The rings' wide glow: only the near-white parts bloom.

The bloom-out. Frame 319 screens a soft lilac over our own city (solved from our base's mean against the source's grey-lavender); then a pale lilac mix, white-cyan, and flat grey-green before the cut.
Ingram's green-blue sky. The fade-up follows the source's measured curve (27% at 0.88 s, 73% at 1.14 s, 92% at 1.41 s); a slow push and drift under everything.

Ingram's replacement mural: the star children walking the winding road toward the star, tilting up from the procession to the star, screened over the sky behind the credit. It fades up over a second, holds, and then leaks into R03: the red star's fade-in (it sits over this) takes it away, so it lasts about five seconds, not two (Ingram: it was too quick to see).
Credit 1: planning and original story. Fade in 1.70-1.95 s, out 4.98-5.13 s (measured).
Ingram's replacement for the round star chart: a red star and a dark world, panning slowly right and pushing in a little; the speed lines fire from the sun's white-hot heart.

Speed lines flying outward, as in the source's R03 and R04, drawn by hand: tapered wedges with uneven, re-drawn edges, on twos. They fire from the exact centre of the chart's star (Ingram: they were off), then from the city lights the camera pushes in on, flying faster and curving slightly as it pushes.

Kurose's coast from the edge of space at dusk (Ingram's R04-city). Like the source's R04, a steady push-in (exponential, so it never slows) toward the brightest cluster of city lights, which lands under the burst's white dot on the burst's frame.
Credit 2: the four founders' original character concepts, credited to the players who made them. In 9.20-9.42 s, out 12.10-12.55 s (measured).

items.text: ピッパ　スティーブ

clips.note: The strobe: a new deep crop of one of Ingram's five smoke stills on every held frame (2.2-3.8x, above the chimneys, so nothing but billows reads), turned, mirrored, alternating washed-out and dark as the source's does. Printed as manga halftone dots (Ingram, 2026-09-26).
The wordmark surfacing grey through the smoke from 13.95 s, in the same place it holds for the rest of the title.
BLΛNK INHERITΛNCE, white on black, held still (14.5-15.9 s).
One frame of pale light nearly filling the frame, a dark-blue wedge low right (the source at 15.96 s).
A great wedge of cyan light from the top, narrowing, as the source's planes do (16.0-16.1 s).
The kanji arriving as blue light with rays rising off every stroke, before they ignite (16.0-16.75 s).
空白相続 ignites: the blade logo, orange to red.
第一部 (Book One) pops in right after the second flare, where the source's small line does (18.17 s).
Lens-flare lines skimming the top of the wordmark (17.83 and 18.05 s).
A blue orb swells behind the logo (19.6 s), then bursts into a ring that runs off the frame.
Crossed beams of light slashing the logo in changing configurations, then the frame washes to white (21.44-21.81 s).
Crane jibs as the source's beam frames: one lattice boom or a crossed pair, dark over the smoke, on single frames. Printed as manga halftone dots (Ingram, 2026-09-26).

Ingram's tall sky, graded deeper (a gamma that darkens the blue and spares the white clouds, toward the source's saturated cel blue, so white credits read), the camera slowly tilting up it for the whole verse so the clouds sink as the newcomer looks up.

Claude's credit (Ingram: 'Claude Code - The Watcher', the role in kanji): 監視者, 'one who keeps watch'. It arrives as the others pass close to camera, in the source's third block's slot (28.87-32.34 s). Why this timeline is never synced. Moved to the foot of the picture, clear of the cards' plates and windows.
The sky dissolves to Ingram's sunset over the chimneys (36.51-36.86 s), framed wide to show most of the city (her note), tilting down a little on threes through R13.
The Frame's green line blueprint over the city, drifting slowly from top to bottom the whole time at one speed (her note), fainter than before, dissolving over the start of R14.

The Watcher, a glimpse (LEDGER #37): Ingram's image, wide enough to keep its context (her note): the great eye, the smaller eyes crowding the sky, the town beneath. A hard cut in, pushing in a little on twos, gone in under a second. It never blinks; it has no eyelids (dossier-observer.md §6).
The honest music credit (Ingram, 2026-09-25), where the source credits its own music (41.1 s): Shiro Sagisu and Masamichi Amano top left, Maurice Jarre (the Directorate's waltz) bottom right.
The honest song credit, in the slot where the source credits its own theme song (43.8 s): lyrics Neko Oikawa, music Hidetoshi Sato, arrangement Toshiyuki Omori, vocals Yoko Takahashi.
Yellow-and-black hazard bands framing the counter panel, as on the source's.
The counters glowing amber: 外部 EXTERNAL showing all eights for a beat, then 内部 INTERNAL counting down over the next, landing on the bar's downbeat (round 14: the cuts follow the kick).
FLASH: Hyuck, the gnoll, teeth bared and the tiny skulls at his throat (Ingram's portrait). Held, then darkened over the last frames in the source's own steps (measured from its R28-R31).
FLASH: Rupiah, the elf, in his red glasses (Ingram's portrait). Held, then darkened over the last frames in the source's own steps (measured from its R28-R31).
FLASH: Anabala, the mitflit, in her wide hat and round glasses (Ingram's portrait). Held, then darkened over the last frames in the source's own steps (measured from its R28-R31).
FLASH: Shucks, the skeleton in his white coat (shown fully, settled 2026-09-25) (Ingram's portrait). Held, then darkened over the last frames in the source's own steps (measured from its R28-R31).

The small mitflit on its rooftop ledge, looking up at the evening sky: Ingram's image on its own, full frame (she likes it too much to lay it over a face). A slow push with a slight pan on threes (her note: it helps it feel alive), drifting the figure right and down, away from the song credit.
Taka waving (Ingram's image, cut out of its flat green), sliding in a little from the right on twos. Simpler than the source's window inset, at Ingram's call, and gone before the Watcher's eye.
The tape catching as it starts: a tracking band rolling up the picture.
A tear as the burst hits.
The white flash tearing into the verse.
A small glitch mid-verse.
The tape tearing as the Watcher appears, and again as it goes: the picture itself flinching from it.

A high-summer heat haze over the rooftop, as if shot through moving ripple glass, strongest just above the hot roofline and fading out up the sky, rising, every frame. Under the credit, so the type stays crisp. History: the first pass (2 px, 38 px across, 55 px/s) was "too subtle"; the second (4.5 px, 14 px, 110 px/s) was too much: Ingram asked for it "softer and less amplitude and slightly slower", so now 2.4 px ripples, 26 px across, rising at 80 px/s.
The stencil now sits on a flat armour-grey card: the plate was a crop of the R23 Frame image, and the same image twice becomes a text card (Ingram).
Stacked, with the initials enlarged, as the source's is.
The Directorate's approved seal, vermilion on black (artwork/emblems/, cut out by Ingram).
The second glimpse of the Watcher: the tentacled shape over the red city (Ingram's xx-07), three frames (LEDGER #37).
The tape flinches at the Watcher again, as at R17.
The acceptance letter's bilingual letterhead (canon: the-road-in brief), with typed lines under it drawn as bars, so no wording is invented.
The blast blossoming on the shore (Ingram's xx-04), pushing in hard.
The rift: a violet aperture with a black core, tearing wider. The land it tears across (Kortos) is still to come as art.
A searchlight burns out to white.

Black on white, as the source's one-word card: the gods' answer from the founding story. The last flash of the montage, five frames long, then the bar line and the quiet (round 15: the Gen 2 head before it is gone).

The director card in the source's L: the role small and upright at the top left, the name large along and then down. It lands with the stripe on the bar line, over the vault (not on a black card of its own), and goes before the light floods it.
A vermilion stripe with black chevrons wiping across, on ones. Now the wipe from the pilot to the vault.
Now the wipe from the pilot to the vault.
The end card's credit fading in, a smaller line beneath the production company's mark: 製作, the production committee. (The wall behind it is painted in code until its art comes.)
Five seconds of fading out after the song (Ingram, 2026-09-26: 'we need a longer tail'), then black. It starts a second after the music ends, so the mark is seen whole in the silence.
A cel-shaded violet sphere with a mottled skin, a rim light and a glow (the source's red core, in the Claimants' colour). A light, not a creature.
Violet lightning crackling off the aperture, re-drawn on twos.
Now the wipe from the pilot to the vault.
A violet enemy machine, red-eyed, against a red wall (Ingram's bad_mech): the source's Angel flash.
A glimpse of Gen 2 being built: a welder at a dark red-eyed head, tilting up (Ingram's gen_02_04).
The cult's beaked mask and violet hood, two frames (Ingram's cultist): the source's red sketch flash.
A coastal gun bunker at sunset, panning along its barrels (Ingram's bunker_pan), before KUROSE.
The agents in caps and dark glasses (Ingram's xx-05), in her own colours, over R56 to R58.
A marksman and his spotter on a rooftop over the city (Ingram's sniper).
A figure in a hospital bed in blue light (Ingram's hospital): the source's face with its eyes opening.
A woman in dark red with a sidelong look (Ingram's bad_guy_woman).
A bald man in split light at a desk (Ingram's bad_guy): the source's sinister council member.
A pale-suited man and his shadow, two frames (Ingram's bad_guy_02): the source's mysterious sketch.
A welder raising the torch as the sparks fly (Ingram's repair animation), over R73-R74 and pushing in toward the torch, so what's happening reads (Ingram: 'so shortened that it's not obvious').
A stately house among old trees (Ingram's posh-house), in the first adventure's run.
A man in a wide hat and tinted glasses (Ingram's Baldwin): the sketch slot's glimpse (LEDGER #37).

A Gen 2 walker by a radar dish on a hill (Ingram's gen_02_03): a whole bar of it, panning slowly left (round 15: it was a quarter of a second, then a radar card). The radar scope and the lock-on that were the next shot lie over it now.

A pilot climbing onto a white machine, tilting down (Ingram's gen_02_05): a whole bar of it, the whole tilt from the machine's head to the pilot (it was a second). The vermilion stripe that opens the next bar wipes it away: only the part ahead of the stripe still shows. A glimpse (LEDGER #37).
The school in summer sun behind Taka (Ingram's school; she asked for Taka on a real background).
The mech bay, panning slowly across and pushing in a little, for five beats (Ingram: it was too brief to see what was happening).
Chorus one opens on the Gen 1 Frame (Ingram's hero plate): one tilt from its molten base up to its green eye.
A gloved hand holding up a glowing power cell (Ingram's battery animation), on twos; moved from R21, where it had five frames.
The conspiracy wall (Ingram's xx-08), pushing in; the 極秘 stamp lands on it, and FIRST IMPACT follows: the secret file on the first impact. Moved from R67.
A battleship's guns under summer clouds, panning (Ingram's battleships_pan): the source's fleet, moved from R61 to where it has room.
The other empty hall, a clock and tall windows (Ingram's xx-02), moved from R57: it stands between Manako and the blast, so nothing follows him straight into it.

A red-eyed machine head swinging round to face us (Ingram's gen_02_01 animation), and its eyes flare as it does, instead of cutting to the eyes in the dark (Ingram, 2026-09-26). A Gen 2 glimpse, under a second.
Two beats each now, so each one registers (Ingram: far too quick): a tracked scout machine in the street (Ingram's military-scout-robot).
Two beats each now, so each one registers (Ingram: far too quick): a tracked machine with a searchlight (Ingram's tank).
Two beats each now, so each one registers (Ingram: far too quick): a wheeled recon carrier against the sunset (Ingram's recon tank).
A Gen 1 dome walker in the street, front-on (Ingram's gen_one_mech_02).
The eye's glow, keyed frame by frame to the pupil as the head turns.
An anamorphic streak through the eye.
The star glint as the eye flares, on the pupil.
The eye's glow, keyed frame by frame to the pupil as the head turns.
An anamorphic streak through the eye.
The star glint as the eye flares, on the pupil.
The flare blooming.
The domed assembly hall at sunset (Ingram's assembly hall): the Directorate's house, before its seal.
The empty hall at dusk, the city in its windows (Ingram's xx-03), tilting up: inside, after hours.
Trainees in ranks against a tower block (Ingram's xx-06): the source's fleet, military might.
Portrait flash: a medic with a red cross armband against the evening sky (Ingram's medic).
Flash: a figure in a long coat and cap against a red sky (Ingram's secret-police).
Portrait flash: a gnoll in profile, one eye glowing (Ingram's gnoll).
A Gen 1 crane rig among the wires at dusk, tilting up its boom (Ingram's gen_one_mech_01), before CRANE RIG / FRAME-00.
Portrait flash: the instructor, arms crossed against the clouds (Ingram's trainer).
A long-barrelled tank in the forest (Ingram's large barrel tank), after the blast.
The temple at sunset (Ingram's temple): the first adventure's temple, without the four.
A planet rising over an alien shore, tilting up (Ingram's alien-world): a glimpse after FIRST IMPACT.

LEAD BEAT 1 (a stand-in face until Anne's own character art comes): the cast card for player 1 of 6, five beats each so every player gets the same time. A portrait of any shape (nothing is cut out) assembles in a slanted window from slats on the beat, a reticle locks onto the face, and plates type the player's name beside the character's (未登録, unregistered, until the character is made). The cards alternate sides.

The sky darkened so the cards' orange type and white frames read on it.

Manako at his tea (Ingram's portrait), a real person the party will meet, in place of the animated newcomer (Ingram: she is uncanny, and not a character in the story). A slow push in; dissolves into the rooftop over R15's first ten frames.
Painted in cream on the darkened armour, sprayed through a stencil. The Directorate's name stamps on the snare.
Painted in cream on the darkened armour, sprayed through a stencil. FRAME 01 stamps on the bar's downbeat (the big hit).
Painted in cream on the darkened armour, sprayed through a stencil. The unit's type stamps on the next kick.

A control panel seen at an angle, in place of the launch tunnel (Ingram): pairs of chevron tabs lock and release from each other, red to green, rising up the panel on the beats and ending with every tab released on the third kick, as the source's launch lamps do.
Noise on the downbeat, as the panel comes up.

Section Officer Vetch (Ingram's portrait), a real person the party meets, for a bar, in place of the third newcomer (Ingram: she is not a real character). One slow push in; his image is not used at R65 any more (no repeats), where the flash is gone.
The face flushes orange as it goes toward the machine (the source's R26).

A fast pan across a wall of the Directorate's own status plates, rulers, crosshairs and interference loops, coming to rest on FRAME 01 (Ingram: the machinery pan was a generic sci-fi space, and the orange screens of the source are the language to speak). Smeared at speed, sharp at rest.

The radar scope and the lock-on reticle (the old R97 card, laid over the picture): the reticle closes on the walker on the downbeat and the readout types on, a line a beat apart; the sweep turns and the contacts flare as it passes. The reticle follows the pan.
The red beacon on the machine's shoulder pulses on each beat, riding the tilt up the frame.
The visor catches the light on the third beat.
The visor catches the light on the third beat.

The bunker's great vault door (Ingram's secret_bunker), a whole bar: a slow push in, the director credit over it, and on beat three the door splits along its seam and slides apart into light, the push quickening into it until the picture is all light (round 15: it was a stripe, a card, and three quick pushes).
Dust in the bunker's light.
The last frames go to pure white, so the next shot comes out of the light.

A young soldier in a witch's hat watching the evening over the airfield (Ingram's war-witch-pan), holding the place of the group shot until the group's own art comes (prompt R104-six): the camera comes round from the horizon and the great cloud to find her, and settles. One shot for the bar where there were five cuts and a strobe.
The picture comes out of the vault's light.
Dust and a few sparks in the evening light.
On the crash a lens flare breaks in at the top right corner: a glint, an anamorphic streak that fades away across the picture, and a few faint ghosts.
A quick dip to black, so the end card comes up out of the dark on the bar line.
The end card's wall: a stained concrete hangar wall in dim red-brown light, painted in code until the real art comes (prompt R111-wall). It comes up out of black on the bar line.

The production company's mark (Mythica Machina, from the studio's own logo file), the focal point of the card, written on from left to right as the last vocal note rises and finishing as the music stops, then held through the silence until the tail fades it out.
A soft gleam rides the leading edge of the writing, brightening the letters as the pen reaches them.
A little dust in the hangar's dim light.
